@copilot Apply the user's requested simplification directly to this existing RPC PR #20879. The user approved replacing awkward interface-default fallback delegation with the direct nullable exception-class expression in four non-HTTP getter-family PRs. This assignment is ONLY this PR; do not create another PR or update other branches.

Keep getErrorType() authoritative for the final error.type and retain its default method. In overrides that fall back to the exception-only getter default, replace the fallback-only interface-qualified super.getErrorType(request, response, error) call with the equivalent direct expression: error == null ? null : error.getClass().getName(). A local guard that already proves the throwable is non-null can simply return its class name. Apply this to affected production overrides and changed test fixtures; preserve ordinary inheritance that performs additional classification rather than merely supplying this fallback. Do not introduce a helper, common base class, cross-domain abstraction, flag, or new API to hide the expression.

Revise the affected RpcAttributesGetter.getErrorType Javadoc so it explains the final-value contract and how an override can return the exception class as fallback without recommending or requiring interface-default delegation. Update this PR's existing breaking-change CHANGELOG entry wherever it mandates or demonstrates such delegation, keeping it concise and not adding a second entry. Keep default exception fallback, no-error null, custom classifications, explicit-null omission, and direct extractor writes exactly as implemented. Delegation remains technically possible, but it is no longer the prescribed migration pattern.

Audit gRPC, both AWS SDK generations, Thrift, and Sofa RPC. Keep preview/duplicate/default emission gating unchanged. In particular, preserve exception-class error.type for the existing gRPC server non-error status with an actual cause without changing its UNSET span status.

This is a behavior-preserving simplification of already verified code. Preserve every existing protocol/service-code precedence rule, selected exception identity, cancellation case, deliberate null omission, _OTHER rule, span status, metrics, lifecycle, and semconv selection. Preserve this PR's current base and draft/ready state. Other getter families, HTTP PR #20881, and held Dubbo PR #20782 are out of scope. HTTP needs its role-specific status/exception/_OTHER default policy and must not be simplified to this expression. Do not implement span-status alignment or make getErrorType mandatory.

Follow CONTRIBUTING.md and applicable repository instructions. Do not add Nullable annotations in test code. Keep focused existing default/custom/null and affected-override tests, adjusting only what this simplification requires. Apply the narrowest applicable spotlessApply directly before the targeted behavioral validation, run relevant central extractor and affected-module tests where feasible, and report genuine blockers without unrelated fixes. Acceptance is no fallback-only super delegation remaining for this getter family in the migrated overrides, equivalent telemetry behavior, and Javadoc/changelog guidance consistent with the direct expression. Leave PR title/body edits and review-thread handling to the coordinator.

@copilot Complete and refresh this existing RPC PR #20879 directly on its existing head branch. Do not create another PR, change its main base or draft state, or update other branches. The user's settled 3.0 contract is that getErrorType() returns the final error.type and null deliberately omits it, even with a Throwable. Keep RpcAttributesGetter.getErrorType as a default method returning error == null ? null : error.getClass().getName(); the shared extractor must not reinterpret null or add fallback.

Audit the current main implementations, including shared/inherited getters, so all existing protocol classifications and exception fallbacks survive the ownership change. In overrides, use direct nullable exception-class fallback where appropriate, not RpcAttributesGetter.super.getErrorType(). A deliberate omission remains null. Preserve gRPC client/server status distinctions, native exception fallback, cancellation behavior, span status, existing RPC mode gating, and matching span/metric classification. Do not introduce automatic span-status/error-type alignment or new protocol classifications.

Status emission is independently handled by #20952, which currently has a clean Copilot review. Do not copy its branch into this PR or implement its status API here. The agreed integration rule is that getErrorType and a response-status getter must not call each other: a general status getter can report success. Reuse a separate raw/error-code helper where extraction genuinely overlaps. If #20952 has merged by the time you work, preserve its genuine-code provenance and helper separation when updating from main.

Refresh this PR against current main where needed by merging main into the PR head, not the reverse, and do not rebase. Record the pre-update head and verify it remains on the first-parent chain before pushing. Keep focused authoritative-null and default/fallback coverage and the concise breaking-change documentation. Follow repository instructions and run narrow formatting and relevant tests. Make only changes needed to finish this contract; if it already fully meets it on current main, explain that instead of adding churn. Do not edit the PR title/description, reply to human comments, resolve unrelated threads, merge PRs, or wait for CI. Stop after scoped changes are committed and pushed.
